#!/bin/bash
#FLUX --queue=xnat
# NOTE: SLURM's '--exclude' directive to avoid specific nodes has been omitted.
# Flux does not have a direct equivalent in batch script directives. Similar
# behavior can be achieved at submission time by creating a hostlist that
# excludes the unwanted nodes.
#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --ntasks=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=64
# NOTE: Flux does not have a --mem-per-cpu option. The total memory for the task
# has been calculated (64 cpus * 8GB/cpu = 512GB) and specified below.
#FLUX --mem-per-task=512G
# NOTE: The --mail-user and --mail-type directives have been omitted as Flux
# does not have a direct equivalent for job status email notifications.
#FLUX --time=1d24h

# NOTE: The SLURM job array tokens %A and %a have been omitted. If this is an array
# job, it should be submitted with 'flux bulksubmit' and the output/error files
# should be named using {id} and {task[id]}.
#FLUX --output=/mnt/beegfs/XNAT/COGITATE/ECoG/phase_2/processed/bids/derivatives/synchrony_analysis/slurm-{id}.out
#FLUX --job-name=synchrony
config=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --config=*)
      config="${1#*=}"
      ;;
    *)
      printf "***************************\n"
      printf "* Error: Invalid argument: ${1}*\n"
      printf "***************************\n"
      exit 1

  esac
  shift
  echo ${participant_id}
  echo ${config}
done

cd /hpc/users/$USER/sw/github/ECoG

module purge; module load Anaconda3/2020.11; source /hpc/shared/EasyBuild/apps/Anaconda3/2020.11/bin/activate; 
conda activate /hpc/users/$USER/.conda/envs/cogitate_ecog

export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/hpc/users/$USER/sw/github/ECoG

python synchrony/synchrony_master.py --config "${config}"

issues: The script specifies an absolute path for its output file (`/mnt/beegfs/...`). It does not contain a command to create the parent directories. If this long path does not exist at job launch, the job will fail immediately because it cannot open its log file.

The argument parsing loop references an undefined variable: `echo ${participant_id}`. This will not cause an error but will produce an empty line in the output, which may be confusing. This appears to be a leftover from a previous version of the script.

The script's execution logic depends on hardcoded, user-specific absolute paths for the working directory (`/hpc/users/$USER/sw/github/ECoG`) and conda environment (`/hpc/users/$USER/.conda/envs/cogitate_ecog`). This makes the script non-portable and likely to fail if run by another user or in a different environment.

The script chains multiple commands on a single line (`module purge; module load ...; source ...`). While valid, this can make the script harder to read and debug. Placing each command on its own line improves clarity.
